modern: From Alexander the grammarian, to refrain from finding fault, and not to scold in a reproachful way those who used any barbarous or ungrammatical or strange-sounding expression; but skilfully to bring in the very expression which ought to have been used, by way of answering, or confirming, or joining in an inquiry about the thing itself, not about the word, or by some other fitting suggestion.
original: From Alexander the grammarian, to refrain from fault-finding, and not in a reproachful way to chide those who uttered any barbarous or solecistic or strange-sounding expression; but dexterously to introduce the very expression which ought to have been used, and in the way of answer or giving confirmation, or joining in an inquiry about the thing itself, not about the word, or by some other fit suggestion.
